html:
Gustav Klimt was an Austrian painter who in 1897 led a group of artists out of Vienna's official academy to found the Vienna Secession. He is the best known painter of Vienna around 1900.

His golden period paintings, such as The Kiss and the portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer, use gold leaf and flat patterns inspired by Byzantine mosaics. His frank pictures of women and the body caused scandals, and his ceiling paintings for the University of Vienna were rejected.

Vienna at that time was a centre of new thinking, from Freud to music and design. Klimt encouraged younger painters such as Egon Schiele. The portrait of Adele, taken by the Nazis, was returned to her heirs in 2006 after a long legal case. He died in 1918, the year Austria-Hungary ended. See Austria.
